text:
A rejected bulk-close should show up as a 400 with the service's reason, not
as a traceback in the application logs.

bulk_close_orders raises ValidationError for the ordinary refusal cases --
account not found, unpaid invoices, draft orders awaiting review. The route
catches that, replies 400 with the service's message, and logs one INFO
line. These tests exist because an earlier version logged the same
ValidationError at ERROR with exc_info attached, which printed a full
traceback for a request that had already been handled correctly and paged
an on-call engineer for nothing (see INFRA-2091).

We also cover the one case where a genuinely unexpected exception occurs:
that one must still be logged with a traceback, because it is a real fault
and not a refusal. See test_an_unexpected_failure_still_reports_a_traceback
below.

Related: test_form_submit_rejection_noise.py covers the same disposal for
the web form's submission path.

Tests for the retry_request helper.

This file pins the backoff schedule: attempt 1 waits 0.1s, attempt 2 waits
0.2s, attempt 3 waits 0.4s, then the helper gives up and re-raises. Tests
mock time.sleep so they run fast, and assert the exact sequence of sleep
calls -- a change to the backoff multiplier must update this file too.

Feature flags controlling the new invoicing pipeline.

Both flags are read only through this module, not through FeatureHelper
directly, so the dependency between them lives in one place. invoicing_v2
selects which pipeline generates invoices; invoicing_custom_terms lets a
tenant customize payment terms and requires invoicing_v2 -- customizing
terms that no engine consults would be misleading. A lookup that fails
resolves to False for both, which is the safe default: unknown means old
pipeline, unknown means no customization.

Session-scoped helpers for the reporting subsystem.

Call build_report_context() before touching any of the ORM objects
returned by the query helpers in this module: they are all attached to a
short-lived session that build_report_context opens, and using them after
it returns raises DetachedInstanceError instead of lazy-loading, unlike
most of the rest of the codebase where detached access is normal.

Timestamp helpers.

Use utc_naive_now() for every naive DateTime column. Passing an aware
datetime into a naive column lets the database driver apply an implicit
timezone cast using the DB session's own TimeZone setting, so the stored
value ends up depending on which session wrote it -- a bug that only shows
up as a few hours of drift and is hard to reproduce locally. Stripping
tzinfo after converting to UTC avoids that entirely. This module also
exports get_current_timestamp_with_timezone() for the aware columns; do
not mix the two helpers on the same column.

Webhook delivery layer.

This module exists because the product team decided customer-facing
webhooks should be delivered out of the main request path so a slow
customer endpoint can never slow down our own API. That decision also
drove the choice of a separate queue rather than a thread pool: a thread
pool shares memory with the request workers and a stuck customer server
could exhaust it, whereas a queue isolates the blast radius entirely. We
also considered and rejected server-sent events for the same isolation
reason.

Figures out whether a given logging call would actually render stack
frames if it ran.

The presence of exc_info isn't the whole question: the logging module
treats a falsy exc_info as absent, so exception(..., exc_info=None) prints
no traceback even though the keyword is there, while a bare exception(...)
does print one because the method defaults exc_info to True. We walk the
AST node, look at its keywords, and decide based on that.
